The Sabrent Rocket 4 is a solid-state drive in the M.2 2280 form factor, launched on March 30th, 2024. It is available in capacities ranging from 1 TB to 2 TB. This page reports specifications for the 1 TB variant. With the rest of the system, the Sabrent Rocket 4 interfaces using a PCI-Express 4.0 x4 connection. The SSD controller is the PS5027-E27T from Phison, a DRAM cache is not available. Sabrent has installed 162-layer TLC NAND flash on the Rocket 4, the flash chips are made by Kioxia. To improve write speeds, a pseudo-SLC cache is used, so bursts of incoming writes are absorbed more quickly. Thanks to support for the fast PCI-Express 4.0 interface, performance is excellent. The Rocket 4 is rated for sequential read speeds of up to 7,400 MB/s and 6,100 MB/s write; random IO reaches 1000K IOPS for read and 850K for writes.At its launch, the SSD was priced at 99 USD. The warranty length is set to five years, which is an excellent warranty period. Sabrent guarantees an endurance rating of 600 TBW, a typical value for consumer SSDs.

Title: Sabrent Rocket 4 1TB Review: DRAM-Less Gen4 Specs, Speed & TBW (2026)

Highlights:
## Quick answer

The Sabrent Rocket 4 1TB is the pick for buyers who want top-of-class Gen4 speed in a single-sided, laptop-and-PS5-friendly package and can live with DRAM-less sustained behavior — TweakTown's ranking of it among the best Gen4 drives is consistent with both its silicon and its measured results.

 Read: 7400 MB/s Write: 6400 MB/s Endurance: 600 TBW Warranty: 5 years Interface: M.2 4.0 x 4 

The refreshed Sabrent Rocket 4 1TB drops the DRAM, goes single-sided and keeps 7,400/6,400 MB/s Gen4 ratings — TweakTown ranked it among the best Gen4 drives.

...

The Sabrent Rocket 4 1TB carries a name that has been around since 2020, but the drive wearing it today is a different machine. The original paired Phison's E16 with DRAM and 96-layer TLC for 5,000/4,400 MB/s; the current revision — SKU SB-RKT4L, sold on Amazon as Rocket 4 DRAM-Less — is a clean-sheet refresh built on Phison's four-channel PS5027-E27T running DRAM-less with Host Memory Buffer, behind Kioxia BiCS6 TLC. The rated numbers moved forward anyway: 7,400 MB/s sequential reads and 6,400 MB/s writes over PCIe 4.0 x4, with 1,000K random-read and 950K random-write IOPS, all on a single-sided M.2 2280 board. It is, component for component, the same silicon Corsair uses in the MP600 Elite.

...

## Endurance, TBW & Warranty

Sabrent warrants the Rocket 4 1TB for five years, and the current product listing states explicitly that no registration is required — a welcome change from older Sabrent SSDs, which needed registration to unlock the full term. The endurance picture is less explicit: Sabrent's product pages leave TBW unpublished for this revision. Tom's Hardware's launch coverage of the refresh put the allocation at 600 TBW per 1 TB of capacity — 600 TBW at this size — and that figure is the best capacity-specific number available. At 20 GB of writes per day, 600 TBW stretches past 80 years, so the warranty term, not the flash, is the practical limit. The MTBF figure is unpublished, and claims run directly through Sabrent's US-based support, a channel with a generally responsive reputation among enthusiasts, subject to standard proof-of-purchase practice.

### Does the Sabrent Rocket 4 1TB have a DRAM cache? 

 No — this is the biggest change from the original. The refreshed Rocket 4 (SKUs SB-RKT4L-1TB and SB-RKT4L-2TB) uses Phison's DRAM-less PS5027-E27T controller with Host Memory Buffer holding the translation tables in system RAM, paired with Kioxia BiCS6 TLC. The 2020 original used a DRAM-equipped E16 design; the Rocket 4 Plus line still carries DRAM on Phison's E18. Despite losing the cache, the refresh's rated speeds and measured low-queue random reads improved over the old drive — TweakTown's verdict placed it among the best Gen4 drives available. 

### What is the TBW endurance of the Rocket 4 1TB? 

 Sabrent's own product pages do not publish a TBW figure for this revision, which is unusual and worth knowing. The best capacity-specific data comes from Tom's Hardware's launch coverage of the refresh, which put the endurance allocation at 600 TBW per 1 TB of capacity — hence 600 TBW here, doubling to 1,200 TBW on the 2 TB model. For scale, at 20 GB of writes per day the 600 TBW budget lasts more than 80 years, so the five-year warranty is the practical limit. The original 2020 Rocket 4 carried a higher 1,800 TBW rating at 1 TB. 

### Sabrent Rocket 4 or Rocket 4 Plus — what is the difference? 

 They are different drives sharing a name. The current Rocket 4 (SB-RKT4L) is the 2024-refresh: Phison's DRAM-less E27T controller, Kioxia BiCS6 TLC, single-sided PCB, capacities of 1 TB and 2 TB, rated 7,400/6,400 MB/s. The Rocket 4 Plus is the older flagship: Phison's DRAM-equipped E18 controller, Micron 176-layer TLC, double-sided at higher capacities, a range stretching from 500 GB to 8 TB, and the line's highest endurance ratings. Choose the Plus for sustained-heavy work and capacities beyond 2 TB; choose the refreshed Rocket 4 for efficiency, laptops, the PS5 and lower price.
